question.text: Let $\overline{\mathrm{V}}, \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}, \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{p}}$ denotes the mean speed, root mean square speed and most probable speed of the molecules each of mass $m$ in an ideal monoatomic gas at absolute temperature T Kelvin. Which statement(s) is/are correct?

options.text: No molecules can have speed greater than $\sqrt{2} V_{r m s}$
No molecules can have speed less than $V_p / \sqrt{2}$
Average kinetic energy of a molecule is $\frac{3}{4} m V_p^2$

solution.text:
$V_{r m s}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M}}$
$V_{a v g}=\sqrt{\frac{8 R T}{\pi M}}$
$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{mp}}=\sqrt{\frac{2 R T}{\mathrm{M}}}, \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{p}} \lt \overline{\mathrm{V}} \lt \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rms}}$
$\mathrm{K} . E=1 / 2 \mathrm{mV}_{\mathrm{rms}}^2=\frac{1}{2} m \frac{3 R T}{M}=\frac{3}{4} m V_p^2$
